messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a KV shard OOM on prod-west-2 around 11:42. Not the usual churn pattern, looks like steady growth on a few keys over ~2h. Dumped a heap and did a quick pprof.
aj: on it. can you drop the pprof link and the shard id?
maria: shard=kv-1007, profiles: https://internal-storage/pprof/kv-1007-3170001122.pb.gz. quick excerpt: 
```
AllocObjects: +1.9M over 90m
Top alloc sites: lru_cache.Put, kv.prefetchPath
Fragmentation metric jumped ~28% before OOM
```
devin: thanks. does this align with the growth we saw in canary earlier?
zara: i pulled tail of logs — multiple 2-3MB payloads for the same key pattern (user:session:*). looks like a single request type is re-populating huge prefixes.
maria: yeah seems like a misconfigured client cache TTL — clients retrying and writing large blobs. putting an immediate guard on prod to reject >1MB values.
aj: good mitigation. i can roll a soft limit on the store: `max_value_bytes=1048576` with a 5% sample reject metric so we can monitor fallout. rolling now. :rocket: 
sre-bot: Incident INC-4321 created for kv-1007 OOM, severity=high. Pager escalations enabled.
devin: for the postmortem follow-ups: can we split into short-term mitigation, medium-term guardrails, and long-term fix? i'll take ownership of the medium-term bucket (behavioral limits + telemetry).
maria: i'll own the immediate remediation (guard roll + hotfix to prefetch path). ETA EOD today for the prod guard.
zara: i'll run targeted profilers across the user:session prefix and extract top offenders. will have a report by tomorrow morning.
aj: i'll create a dashboard charting value size histograms + per-key churn. need that to validate the 1MB cap doesn't spike client errors.
devin: long-term: we should consider shard-residency eviction heuristics + TTL enforcement at ingress. i'll propose a design doc this week. owner: devin. target: next sprint planning (two weeks).
maria: action item summary: 
- maria: roll guard to reject >1MB and apply canary 10% -> 100% if ok (ETA same day)
- aj: dashboard + reject-sample metric (ETA 24h)
- zara: targeted profiler + offender list (ETA 24h)
- devin: design doc for eviction & ingress TTL (ETA 2w)
- ops: add alert on fragment_ratio > 20% per-shard (requesting infra)

can we add explicit done-by dates to the ticket? helps followups.
aj: added due dates to INC-4321 and linked dashboards.
sre-bot: Note: automatic GC pressure autoscale enabled on affected fleet.
zara: small observation — GC runs reduced resident set but fragmentation remained. suggests large live objects vs alloc churn. need to prioritize reducing object size.
maria: agree. short term we can compress payloads for session objects server-side if clients can't be fixed quickly. aj you ok with a compression proxy?
aj: compression is fine but let's watch CPU. add it as a feature flag behind canary. i'll stash the flag toggle in config: `kv.compress_large_values=true` feature_flag_id=ff/kv-compress.
devin: also please keep a recurring retrospective check for this incident class — set a fortnightly triage for 'kv-residency spikes' and attach one owner each run.
aj: created recurring calendar invite 'kv-residency triage' weekly, owners rotating: maria -> zara -> devin. first meeting next Tue.
maria: quick question — do we want to add a hard slab-eviction if fragment_ratio > 35% for 5m? dangerous but could prevent OOM cascade.
devin: i'd prefer soft measures first (reject + compression) and only slab-evict as emergency last resort. add runbook decision points to the ticket.
zara: logging note: when we reject >1MB, ensure response includes the key pattern and a correlation id so customer teams can debug.
aj: done — reject payload includes `x-kv-reject-reason: size_limit` and `x-kv-correlation-id`.
sre-bot: Update: INC-4321 severity lowered to medium after successful 1MB guard canary.
maria: thanks all. i'll post final remediation checklist to the postmortem doc and close the incident after verifying no regressions for 72h. :white_check_mark:
devin: assign follow-up items in the postmortem to the owners above and include acceptance criteria (dashboard trends, no rejects >0.5% after 72h, fragmentation trending down).
aj: noted — will update.
zara: i'll attach profiler flamegraphs to the postmortem and label offenders with suggested owners.
maria: great. closing notes: recurring pattern flagged — create a small test harness that simulates large-key churn so we can run it in CI against new KV changes. owner: qa-team (cc @qa).
devin: perfect. thanks everyone.
aj: 👍
sre-bot: Incident INC-4321 closed (transitions: high->medium->resolved).
